summary.text: A 12-year-old boy with severe rheumatic heart disease had mitral, tricuspid and aortic valve repair at age 9, then haemolytic anaemia, jaundice and mitral regurgitation, and mitral valve replacement with a 25 mm On-X valve, anticoagulated with warfarin. Three months before presentation his prosthetic valve function was normal. Weighing 75 kg (BMI 31), he presented to a regional Emergency Department with acute pulmonary oedema after diving into water from about 2 m.

The timeline table records presentation with cardiogenic shock; he was normotensive (123/67) but tachycardic, tachypnoeic and desaturated with a mechanical first heart sound, loud apical murmurs and bilateral mid-zone crepitations; INR was 2.9. Transthoracic echocardiography on admission gave a mean mitral inflow gradient of 20 mmHg without obvious regurgitation but limited valve assessment. He deteriorated, was intubated and ventilated with inotropes, and transoesophageal echocardiography showed an absent mechanical valve leaflet with severe mitral regurgitation.

Over the following two hours his respiratory and circulatory support needs escalated and he underwent urgent mechanical mitral valve replacement with a 27 mm St. Jude prosthesis; the right-sided leaflet was absent at surgery. CT three days following surgery showed a fractured leaflet in two segments at the abdominal aortic bifurcation and right common iliac artery, left in situ with no impaired lower limb perfusion.

He was discharged 14 days after the initial presentation without complication and was well at 3-month follow-up; the report states he is asymptomatic three months post-discharge and survived the leaflet escape. The authors state the mechanism of fracture is unknown and propose leaflet fracture with embolisation, possibly through rapid deceleration on diving.
